stories.headline: STMicroelectronics enters high-volume production of silicon photonics platform for AI data centers

key_facts.fact: STMicroelectronics announced on March 9 that it is entering high-volume production of its PIC100 silicon photonics platform on 300mm manufacturing lines, producing 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers for hyperscaler data centers and AI clusters.
key_facts.excerpt: STMicroelectronics is now entering high-volume production for its state-of-the-art silicon photonics-based PIC100 platform used by hyperscalers for optical interconnect for data centers and AI clusters. The 800G and 1.6T PIC100 transceivers enable higher bandwidth, lower latency, and greater energy efficiency as AI workloads surge.

key_facts.fact: ST plans to more than quadruple PIC100 production capacity by 2027, with further expansion in 2028, underpinned by long-term customer capacity reservation commitments.
key_facts.excerpt: Looking ahead, we are planning and executing on capacity expansions to enable more than quadrupling of production by 2027. This fast expansion is fully underpinned by customers' long-term capacity reservation commitments.

key_facts.fact: The data center pluggable optics market reached $15.5 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow at a 17% CAGR from 2025 through 2030, surpassing $34 billion by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The data center pluggable optics market continues to expand strongly, reaching $15.5 billion in 2025. We expect the market to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 17% from 2025 through 2030, surpassin

key_facts.fact: ST also unveiled a PIC100 through-silicon via (TSV) technology roadmap to increase optical connectivity density and support emerging architectures such as near-packaged optics and co-packaged optics.
key_facts.excerpt: STMicroelectronics is developing the PIC100 TSV platform, incorporating through-silicon via technology to increase optical connectivity density and system-level integration.

stories.headline: Nexperia's Chinese subsidiary begins 12-inch wafer chip production, deepening split with Dutch parent

key_facts.fact: Nexperia's Chinese subsidiary announced on March 9 that it has begun producing its own chips using 12-inch wafers — a size the Dutch parent company cannot manufacture in Europe — marking a further step toward independence.
key_facts.excerpt: Nexperia China said it has started making several types of chips also produced by Nexperia, but using 12-inch wafers - a size the Dutch company cannot manufacture in Europe.

key_facts.fact: Nexperia has been in a standoff with its owner Wingtech (600745.SS) and the Nexperia China subsidiary since October 2025, after the Dutch government intervened to block the company from shifting operations to China.
key_facts.excerpt: Nexperia has been in a standoff with both its owner Wingtech and the Nexperia China subsidiary since October 2025, after an intervention by the Dutch government aimed at blocking the company from shifting operations to China.

key_facts.fact: Before the intervention, Nexperia produced wafers in Europe and packaged them into chips in China. The fracture led Nexperia China to declare independence, while Nexperia Europe halted wafer shipments to China citing nonpayment.
key_facts.excerpt: Before the intervention, Nexperia produced wafers in Europe and packaged them into chips in China. Afterwards, the company fractured, with Nexperia China declaring independence and Nexperia Europe halting wafer shipments to China, citing nonpayment.

key_facts.fact: Nexperia China achieved small-batch production of 12-inch wafer bipolar discrete devices, which it called a significant milestone in independent research, development, and mass production capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Nexperia's Chinese subsidiary has announced the successful small-batch production of 12-inch wafer bipolar discrete devices. The company declared this achievement a significant milestone, highlighting its independent research, development, and mass production capabilities.

stories.headline: Amazon's Zoox expands robotaxi testing to Dallas and Phoenix, opens Fusion Center command hub

key_facts.fact: Zoox announced on March 9 it is expanding testing to Dallas and Phoenix, deploying retrofitted Toyota Highlander SUVs for manual mapping before progressing to autonomous testing with safety drivers.
key_facts.excerpt: Zoox is now mapping the streets of Dallas, Texas, and Phoenix, Arizona, as a precursor to testing its autonomous vehicles in the two Sun Belt cities.

key_facts.fact: The expansion takes Zoox's US testing footprint to 10 cities, alongside Atlanta, Austin, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Miami, San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, and Washington, D.C.
key_facts.excerpt: The move will expand testing operations to 10 markets across the country, Zoox said on Monday, adding the two Sun Belt cities to existing sites including Las Vegas, the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, Austin, Miami, Los Angeles, Atlanta and Washington, D.C.

key_facts.fact: Zoox will launch a 'Fusion Center' facility in Scottsdale, Arizona, to serve as a command hub for fleet operations, remote guidance, and rider support, creating hundreds of new jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: Zoox will also open new depots in both cities and launch a 'Fusion Center' facility in Scottsdale, Arizona, to serve as a command hub for fleet operations, remote guidance and rider support. The expansion is expected to create hundreds of jobs.

key_facts.fact: Zoox has driven more than one million autonomous miles in Las Vegas and San Francisco and ferried more than 300,000 passengers through its early-rider program.
key_facts.excerpt: Zoox expands US robotaxi testing to Phoenix and Dallas as autonomous miles surpass 1 million.

key_facts.fact: Zoox is still awaiting federal approval for its purpose-built steering-wheel-free robotaxi, which does not comply with current federal safety standards and requires an NHTSA exemption.
key_facts.excerpt: Because the vehicle cannot comply with federal safety standards, Zoox requires an NHTSA exemption to deploy it commercially.

stories.headline: NHTSA hosts national AV safety forum with Waymo, Zoox, and Aurora CEOs to shape robotaxi regulation

key_facts.fact: NHTSA will host a National AV Safety Forum on March 10 at USDOT Headquarters in Washington, D.C., from 8:50 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. ET, featuring keynote addresses and executive panel discussions on autonomous driving systems.
key_facts.excerpt: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has announced it will host a national autonomous vehicle safety forum on 10 March in Washington.

key_facts.fact: The forum features a fireside chat between NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison and the CEOs of Waymo (Tekedra Mawakana), Zoox (Aicha Evans), and Aurora (Chris Urmson), discussing the path from AV demonstration to commercial scaling.
key_facts.excerpt: NHTSA holds its National AV Safety Forum on March 10 in Washington, D.C., a day-long session that will feature a fireside chat between NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison and the chief executives of Waymo, Zoox, and Aurora.

key_facts.fact: Tesla is present at the venue's AV Showcase on Automation Plaza but is not included in the CEO-level executive panel discussion, reflecting its different regulatory status compared to commercial-scale autonomous operators.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla is listed on the venue's AV Showcase on Automation Plaza outside but is not included in the executive panel discussion with NHTSA.

key_facts.fact: Waymo has accumulated 200 million autonomous miles and provides 400,000 weekly rides across major US markets, highlighting the growing real-world presence of robotaxis.
key_facts.excerpt: Waymo's scale of 200 million autonomous miles and 400,000 weekly rides highlights the growing real-world presence of robotaxis in major U.S. markets.

key_facts.fact: The forum aims to gather stakeholder input on potential federal guidance for the safe development, testing, and deployment of autonomous driving systems, building on a November 2025 AV Workshop.
key_facts.excerpt: Executives from Waymo, Zoox and Aurora will take the stage at an NHTSA event in Washington as the agency moves to finally update federal AV guidelines.

stories.headline: WeRide and Geely's Farizon to deliver 2,000 purpose-built robotaxis by end of 2026

key_facts.fact: WeRide signed an expanded strategic cooperation agreement with Geely's Farizon on March 9, announcing plans to deliver 2,000 upgraded, purpose-built Robotaxi GXRs by end of 2026, with production starting in Q3 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The two companies announced plans to deliver 2,000 upgraded, purpose-built, mass-produced Robotaxi GXRs by 2026, advancing WeRide's progress toward large-scale global Robotaxi commercialization.

key_facts.fact: As of January 2026, WeRide's global robotaxi fleet had 1,023 vehicles; with the 2,000 new units, the fleet is expected to surpass 2,600 vehicles this year, with a long-term target of tens of thousands by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: As of January 2026, WeRide's global Robotaxi fleet had 1,023 vehicles. With the addition of 2,000 new Robotaxi GXRs, WeRide expects its global operating Robotaxi fleet to surpass 2,600 Robotaxis this year.

key_facts.fact: The upgraded GXR uses WeRide's GEN8 autonomous driving system with a thousand-line LiDAR providing 17x improvement in point-cloud resolution and 600-meter detection range — 2 to 3 times the industry standard.
key_facts.excerpt: The vehicle's core sensors include a new-generation lidar with a maximum detection range of up to 600 meters.

key_facts.fact: Production efficiency per vehicle will be reduced from around one hour to under 10 minutes by leveraging Geely Farizon's manufacturing system, with overall vehicle costs expected to decline about 15%.
key_facts.excerpt: The production cycle per vehicle is projected to be reduced from around one hour to less than 10 minutes. At the same time, overall vehicle costs are expected to decline by about 15% compared with the previous model.

key_facts.fact: WeRide currently operates fully driverless services in Guangzhou, Beijing, and Abu Dhabi, with public passenger services in Dubai and Riyadh, and a Singapore public launch scheduled for April 1, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Fully driverless services in: Guangzhou, Beijing, Abu Dhabi. Public passenger services in: Dubai, Riyadh. Trial operations: Singapore (public launch April 1, 2026).

stories.headline: SpaceX launches EchoStar XXV satellite on its 30th mission of 2026, Dish's first new sat in 16 years

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the EchoStar XXV direct broadcast satellite from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 12:19 a.m. EDT on March 10, after an hour-long delay, marking SpaceX's 30th mission of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifts off from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station to begin the EchoStar-25 mission on March 9, 2026.

key_facts.fact: EchoStar XXV is Dish Network's first new broadcast satellite in 16 years; it will operate at 110 degrees west longitude in geostationary orbit, delivering television content across North America.
key_facts.excerpt: Dish's first new broadcast satellite in 16 years. From this vantage point above the Pacific, EchoStar XXV will deliver television content across North America.

key_facts.fact: The Falcon 9 first-stage booster (B1085) was making its 14th flight, and SpaceX's 600th booster recovery attempt, landing on the droneship 'A Shortfall of Gravitas' in the Atlantic Ocean.
key_facts.excerpt: B1085 Flight #14. 600th recovery attempt.

key_facts.fact: The satellite was built on the Maxar 1300 series platform by Lanteris Space Systems at facilities in Palo Alto and San Jose, weighing approximately 6,800 kg (15,000 lbs).
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX launches 15,000-pound TV satellite to orbit on its 30th mission of the year.

stories.headline: Chinese researchers unveil OmniXtreme framework enabling humanoid robots to perform backflips and martial arts

key_facts.fact: Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence (BIGAI) and Unitree Robotics published the OmniXtreme framework, enabling humanoid robots to learn dozens of high-dynamic movements including backflips, Thomas flairs, and martial arts kicks with over 90% success rates.
key_facts.excerpt: Success rates exceeding 90% across multiple high-dynamic tasks. Implements 'one algorithm to control multiple movements.'

key_facts.fact: OmniXtreme uses a two-stage approach: a flow-based generative control policy pre-trained via knowledge distillation from expert policies, followed by actuation-aware residual reinforcement learning for real-world transfer on Unitree G1 robots.
key_facts.excerpt: OmniXtreme框架的实现过程首先是预训练一个基于流的生成控制策略, 然后针对复杂物理动力学进行驱动感知残差强化学习的后训练。

key_facts.fact: The framework is the first universal policy capable of executing various extreme actions, overcoming the 'generality barrier' where traditional unified reinforcement learning strategies suffer performance collapse as the number and diversity of actions increase.
key_facts.excerpt: 该框架是首个可以执行各种极限动作的通用策略, 人形机器人学习复杂运动方式带来明显提效解决了动作保真度与可扩展性兼顾的难题。

key_facts.fact: The research team includes contributors from BIGAI, Unitree Robotics, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, with corresponding authors Jia Baoxiong and Huang Siyuan from BIGAI.
key_facts.excerpt: 通研院研究员贾宝雄、黄思远。

stories.headline: Waymo, Wayve, and Baidu to test robotaxis in London as UK government launches spring pilot program

key_facts.fact: The UK government's robotaxi trials are set to launch in the spring of 2026 in London, with Wayve Technologies, Waymo, and Baidu planning to participate in the pilot program.
key_facts.excerpt: The autonomous vehicle from British startup Wayve Technologies is on a test run ahead of the U.K. government's robotaxi trials set to launch in the spring. Tech companies including U.S. company Waymo and China's Baidu also plan to take part in the pilot program.

key_facts.fact: Wayve is already testing Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles equipped with onboard AI systems on London streets, navigating jaywalkers, cyclists, and roadwork in complex traffic conditions.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ford Mustang Mach-E cruises down a London road choked with traffic, using its onboard AI system to avoid jaywalkers and cyclists, and navigate roadwork as it drives to its destination.

key_facts.fact: London's ancient road layout dating back to Roman times poses unique challenges compared to American grid cities, with black cab drivers' union calling robotaxis 'a solution looking for a problem.'
key_facts.excerpt: Self-driving taxis are 'a solution looking for a problem,' said Steven McNamara, general secretary of the Licensed Taxi Drivers' Association, which represents black cabbies.

stories.headline: UK's planned 1GW AI data center campus would emit 1M tonnes of CO2 annually, planning vote March 11

key_facts.fact: Planning documents revealed on March 9 that the Elsham Tech Park, a proposed £10 billion AI data center campus on a former RAF base near Scunthorpe in Lincolnshire, would generate annual CO2 emissions of approximately one million tonnes — on par with a year of British Airways short-haul flights.
key_facts.excerpt: Planning documents for a £10 billion project in Lincolnshire reveal its annual emissions will reach one million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

key_facts.fact: The data center campus would consume approximately 3.7 billion kWh of electricity annually and comprise up to 15 individual data center buildings totaling up to 1GW capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Documents estimate the datacentre would consume 3.7bn kWh of energy.

key_facts.fact: The North Lincolnshire planning committee is scheduled to vote on the application on March 11, 2026; the total investment could reach £5.5-7.5 billion over multiple phases.
key_facts.excerpt: Planning committee 11 March 2026.

key_facts.fact: Developers argue the site sits within the UK's most advanced clean energy cluster, with access to a third of the nation's offshore wind capacity and two-thirds of licensed carbon capture and storage sites.
key_facts.excerpt: A single AI data centre would generate annual carbon emissions on a par with a year of British Airways short-haul flights.
